name: causal_grounding_v5_crossfit_mannwhitney_colspec_optional
purpose: Fraction of genetic perturbations for which a control-trained SAE is causally grounded on Perturb-seq, comparing expression-space vs foundation-model-embedding SAEs.
trained_on: control (non-targeting) cells only; SAE never sees a perturbation
feature_program: gene-association profile = Pearson corr of feature activation with each gene over control cells (identical for expression- and embedding-space SAEs)
matchable_features: only features active in >= min_active_cells control cells are matchable (near-dead features have unreliable programs)
cross_fitting: each tested perturbation's cells are split A|B (random half, seeded). The feature is MATCHED on split A and the suppression test is run on the held-out split B, so the same cells never both select and validate the feature (removes double-dipping / selection bias).
matching_rule: on split A: perturbation p (KD of gene t) is matched to argmax over matchable features of dot(program_normalized, -DE_signature_normalized); the KD gene t is EXCLUDED from both the program and the DE signature (program-level, non-trivial)

grounding_rule.match_confidence: matched program alignment is a robust-z (median/MAD) upper-tail outlier vs alignment to all OTHER matchable features; match_confidence_p < match_alpha (excludes diffuse/global perturbations)
grounding_rule.suppression: one-sided Mann-Whitney U of the matched feature's activation in p's split-B knockdown cells vs all control cells (alternative='less'); AUC = U / (n_kd_B * n_ctrl); AUC < 0.5 = suppressed
grounding_rule.column_specificity: p suppresses the matched feature MORE than other perturbations do: p's mean split-B activation of the feature is a robust-z (median/MAD) LOWER-tail outlier vs the mean activation of that feature across all OTHER tested perturbations; colspec_p < colspec_alpha. Rejects non-specific stressors (e.g. essential-gene knockdowns) that drop a shared feature many knockdowns also drop.
grounding_rule.colspec_alpha: DEFAULT 1.0 = OFF (v5 rollback; set 0.10 to enable). Column specificity removed a genuine regulator (GATA1) on real Replogle without removing the housekeeping hits.
grounding_rule.multiple_testing: Benjamini-Hochberg FDR across tested perturbations on the Mann-Whitney p-values
grounding_rule.grounded_iff: passes_match (match_confidence_p < match_alpha) AND passes_floor (auc <= effect_floor_auc) AND BH-q(mw_p) < fdr  [column specificity optional, default off]

global_specificity: the pipeline runs a label-shuffle permutation null (n_shuffle relabelings): the observed causal_grounding_rate must exceed the shuffled null. Global chance control is at the pipeline level, not per-perturbation.
primary_comparison: expression-space causal_grounding_rate vs embedding-space rate; positive result iff expression >> embedding (target: a multiple of the published 6.2-10% embedding ceiling), robust across >=5 seeds
control_label: control (mapped from the dataset's control value, e.g. 'non-targeting')
frozen_before: any run on real Replogle data

what_changed: Suppression measure: standardized activation drop (effect_floor 0.25 SD) REPLACED by one-sided Mann-Whitney AUC (effect_floor_auc 0.45).
Added cross-fitting: match on split A, test suppression on held-out split B.
Split match confidence and suppression into two independent gates (was combined via max(p) into one BH-FDR family).
amendments.why: Two bugs caught on synthetic BEFORE any real Replogle result. (1) SD-standardization is invalid for sparse TopK activations: a feature fires in ~k/L of cells, so even a full shutoff is only ~0.1 SD, unreachable by any effect floor -> forced 0 grounded. A rank-based Mann-Whitney AUC has no scale assumption. (2) Without cross-fitting the same cells both selected and validated a feature, letting diffuse/background perturbations appear grounded (double-dipping). Fix validated on synthetic: oracle unit test passes (true regulators grounded, null/global/background rejected), and real-vs-shuffle shows planted regulators grounded with 0 false positives vs a shuffled null of 0.000.
amendments.honesty_note: No valid result on real data was produced under v1; nothing was frozen or reported from the buggy metric. This amendment is dated and pre-registered before the first valid real run, per the project's no-frozen-artifact-from-a-broken-run rule.

what_changed: Added gate (3) COLUMN SPECIFICITY: p must suppress the matched feature more than other perturbations do (colspec_p < colspec_alpha=0.10), a robust-z lower-tail outlier test on per-perturbation mean feature activation.
amendments.why: The v3 (single-seed) Replogle run grounded a set ~10x enriched for Hart CEGv2 core-essential genes (8/26 seed-stable hits vs 3.0% base rate, hypergeometric p~4e-7; docs/COMPONENT2_RESULTS.md). Diagnosis: v3 tested suppression only vs CONTROL, so an essential-gene knockdown that collapses transcription globally drops a shared 'cell-health' feature that many knockdowns also drop, and each such knockdown passed independently. The label-shuffle null controls the global RATE but not per-perturbation specificity. Column specificity restores the per-perturbation specificity the v3 cross-fit rewrite had dropped (it was in the original v1 design intent). Validated on synthetic (tests/test_causal_grounding.py::test_column_specificity): with the gate OFF, 5 shared non-specific stressors falsely ground; with it ON, all 5 are rejected while the true sole-regulators survive. The existing oracle + pipeline self-tests still pass unchanged.
amendments.honesty_note: The v3 single-seed run was logged as PRELIMINARY and explicitly NOT frozen (docs/COMPONENT2_RESULTS.md). This v4 amendment is dated and made before any frozen/reported real result, per the no-frozen-artifact-from-a-confounded-run rule. Column specificity is deliberately conservative: it also rejects genuinely redundant regulators (a program with several real regulators), which is an accepted trade for killing the essential-gene confound; that limitation is documented.

what_changed: Column specificity DEFAULT OFF (colspec_alpha 0.10 -> 1.0). Still available via --colspec-alpha.
grounded_iff reverts to match AND floor AND FDR (three gates).
amendments.why: The v4 column-specificity gate FAILED on real Replogle. Multi-seed run: it removed GATA1 (the one lineage regulator, from >=3/5 seeds down to 2/5) while leaving the entire housekeeping/machinery set intact. Root cause: the synthetic confound modelled MANY perturbations suppressing ONE shared feature (which the gate catches), but the real structure is each essential-gene KD suppressing its OWN distinct stress feature where it genuinely is the top suppressor (which the gate passes) -- and, separately, a program with multiple real regulators (like GATA1's erythroid program in K562) makes GATA1 look non-specific and gets it wrongly cut. So the gate removed real signal without removing the confound. Rolled back to avoid actively suppressing genuine regulators.
amendments.honesty_note: Also correcting an earlier overstatement: the '~10x essential-gene enrichment (p~4e-7)' in an earlier note used the WRONG background (all 1839 TFs, ~3% essential). Against the correct background (the 162 tested TFs, ~31% essential -- the Replogle ESSENTIAL library is essential-gene-dominated by construction), essential and non-essential perturbations ground about EQUALLY (11.8% vs 12.6%). There is no essential-gene PREFERENCE; the grounded set is housekeeping-heavy because the tested pool is. The real finding is that grounding tracks perturbation EFFECT-DETECTABILITY, not regulatory specificity, on this dataset. See docs/COMPONENT2_RESULTS.md.
